mappings.note: A leaking pipe reported to the ward committee: knowing which urban body handles it (LO-271) and acting as a participating citizen (CG-SST3).
Preparing questions for a visiting urban local body member about their role and duties - the functioning of urban bodies, so LO-271.
Collecting neighbours' expectations of the urban local body; what these bodies are supposed to deliver, hence LO-271.
Lists the marks of a good urban local body - a judgement about how such bodies should function, so LO-271.
Panchayati Raj set against urban local bodies: LO-271 covers rural AND urban local bodies together, which is exactly what this comparison needs.
Names participatory democracy as the idea of citizens shaping their country's working - a democratic concept, so the goal rather than a local-body outcome.
Why urban governance is more complex - density, diversity and infrastructure; a claim about how urban bodies must work, so LO-271.
Indore's cleanliness credited to citizens as well as the Corporation: the urban body's sanitation work (LO-271) together with civic participation (CG-SST3).
Local bodies existing to give governance from the grassroots - the role of government at the local level (LO-269) as a democratic principle (CG-SST3).
The short-answer version of why urban governance is more complex; same demand as the multiple-choice item, so LO-271.
Ward committees running health camps and reporting damaged roads and leaks - the working of an urban local body in health and infrastructure, which LO-271 names.
Three functions of urban local bodies - garbage, roads, local taxes; the remit of these bodies, so LO-271.
How citizens make the urban body more efficient by segregating waste and reporting faults: the body's work (LO-271) depending on civic participation (CG-SST3).
Recalls 'participatory democracy' as the wider idea; a democratic concept, hence CG-SST3.
Names urban local bodies as the town and city structures of local government - the basic term, so LO-271.
What 'decentralised' means - local communities deciding for themselves rather than a central authority: the principle (LO-269) as it applies to urban bodies (LO-271).
Wards as the units into which towns are divided for local governance; a structure item inside urban local government, so LO-271.
Names a ward committee activity such as a health camp or anti-plastic campaign - urban local body work in health, which LO-271 covers.
Names an infrastructure fault a ward committee would report; the body's monitoring function, so LO-271.
Lists one urban local body function from infrastructure, burial grounds, garbage or taxes - the remit of these bodies, hence LO-271.
The Madras Corporation's founding date of 1688; a fact about India's oldest municipal institution, so LO-271 rather than a history outcome.
The East India Company's charter creating the Fort St George corporation - the origin of the urban local body, so LO-271.
The 1792 Act giving the Madras Corporation power to levy municipal taxes: the body's taxation function, which is part of how urban local bodies work.
Indore as the cleanest city under Swachh Survekshan - a named urban body's sanitation record, so LO-271.
Municipal Corporation as the body for cities above ten lakh; the tiering of urban local bodies by population, so LO-271.
Municipal Council or Nagar Palika for towns of one to ten lakh - the middle band of the same classification.
Nagar Panchayat for the smallest towns; the third band of the urban local body classification, so LO-271.
Anita placed as the city child in the chapter's dialogue - the urban half of the rural-urban comparison the conversation is built on, so LO-271.
Sameer likening the city's system to his village Panchayat, only bigger: the rural-urban comparison of local bodies, which LO-271 spans.
Children reporting a dangerously low electricity wire to a Gram Sabha member - a local body responding to a citizen report; LO-271 covers rural bodies too.
Why the urban system must be more elaborate, at short-answer length; mapped with the other complexity items under LO-271.
Sidhwa on local bodies teaching people their rights: constitutional rights and democratic learning (CG-SST3) through the local government (LO-269).
How urban bodies teach administration, franchise and rights in practice - democratic education (CG-SST3) delivered by the urban local body (LO-271).
Sets out the specific urban complexities - density, varied needs, infrastructure, pollution - that force a more intricate structure, so LO-271.
Gram Sabha against Ward Committee at the base of the governance pyramid: two local bodies compared (LO-271) as forms of grassroots democracy (CG-SST3).
The two-way bargain between citizen duty and municipal efficiency - the body's performance (LO-271) resting on civic participation (CG-SST3).

A damaged item whose supplied answer is a case on a Municipal Council raising property tax after public consultation: the urban body's funding (LO-271) and consultation as democratic practice (CG-SST3).
Why a child's voice carries further in a village than in a city, and what Ward Committees do about it: scale of the local bodies (LO-271) against accessibility of democracy (CG-SST3).
Air pollution, weak municipal enforcement and citizen groups using RTI: the Corporation's regulatory function (LO-271) met by participatory democracy (CG-SST3).
How urban local elections let citizens exercise the franchise and learn their rights: democratic practice (CG-SST3) through ward representatives (LO-271).
